title: Solomon
summary: Solomon belongs to Israel's monarchy or royal transition and helps trace kingship, judgment, and messianic hope.
historical_context: Solomon appears in the rise, division, or decline of Israel's kingdoms, where royal power and covenant accountability collide.
ancient_near_east_context: Royal courts, dynastic succession, warfare, and imperial pressure shape the background.
literary_context: Samuel, Kings, and Chronicles use Solomon to narrate leadership, covenant faithfulness, and judgment.
covenantal_significance: Solomon contributes to the royal line and the Bible's questions about faithful kingship.
interpretive_notes: Do not flatten monarchy into simple success or failure; the narratives often hold both together.
Royal stories are always read against covenant accountability.
